newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Argentina says WTO aspirants must trade freely.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says WTO aspirants must trade freely.

text.p: The Cairns Group of agricultural exporting nations should seek to ensure that aspiring members of the World Trade Organization (WTO) open their markets, Argentina's agriculture secretary said on Friday.

In addition to concerns over barriers to agricultural exports maintained by existing members of the WTO, the group's members are concerned about China and Russia, which are seeking to join the organization, Felipe Carlos Sola said.
"The countries which are joining up do not offer the right kind of concessions for trade. They want to join at no cost. without improving the market," Sola told reporters.

Argentina presented the Cairns Group meeting with a study on the trade policies of the WTO aspirants. Sola also criticized the United States for not taking the concerns of other countries into account when negotiating over trade, particularly in the case of China.

"The U.S. sorts out its problems and then expects everyone else to receive the new countries with open arms when in fact we lose out," he said. "We don't want countries joining the WTO to be subject to conditions less strict than those for existing members."
The 15 members of the Cairns Group account for about 20 percent of global agriculture exports. The group includes Australia, Canada and New Zealand as well as a dozen developing nations.
((-- Julio Villaverde, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
